rich_summary: Kaikeyi reveals to Bharata that she demanded two boons from King Dasharatha: the exile of Rama and the installation of Bharata as heir. The king obeyed his promise but died of grief after Rama departed with Sita and Lakshmana. Rather than rejoice, Bharata is devastated and furious. He condemns his mother’s ambition, accusing her of destroying the king, shaming the Ikshvaku dynasty, and exiling the righteous Rama who loved her like a mother. Bharata insists the throne belongs by sacred custom to the eldest son and rejects the kingdom gained through injustice. Declaring he will never fulfill Kaikeyi’s wishes, he vows to bring Rama back from the forest and serve him. The episode establishes Bharata’s moral greatness and loyalty, reinforcing the epic’s central theme of dharma over power.

highlight_spans.why: Kaikeyi’s confession that she engineered Rama’s exile and Bharata’s succession, setting up the moral crisis.
Bharata’s first anguished response, mourning his father and condemning the act that banished Rama.
Bharata appeals to the ancient law of the Ikshvaku house: the eldest son must rule, emphasizing dharma over ambition.
Bharata’s decisive vow that he will bring Rama back from the forest and serve him rather than take the throne.

top_scenes.scene_text: Prince Bharata, blazing with anger and grief, confronts Queen Kaikeyi in the royal chamber while courtiers watch in stunned silence.
Bharata roaring like a lion as he denounces his mother, his arm raised in oath within the shadowed halls of Ayodhya’s palace.
